[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
John was born about 1766. He passed away in 1836. "On the 28th ult. Mr John Glasgow, of Cross, near Broughshane, in the 70th year of his age. He died as he lived, a steady, sincere Christian'<ref>https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/227263750/john-glasgow</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Bannside origin and the Crawford landlord question ===

PRONI’s description of the Crawford Papers identifies [[Glasgow-1657|John Glasgow]] as a weaver from the Bannside, married to [[McClure-6341|Jean or Jane McClure]] from Drumack in the Braid. Their son [[Glasgow-1780|James McClure Glasgow]] was born near Clough on 27 May 1805 and was the third of seven children. The description gives no earlier Glasgow parent or exact Bannside holding.<ref name="CrawfordD2003Scope">PRONI, ''Crawford Papers (D2003), Introduction'', November 2007, [https://www.sommemidulster.org/dwd/pdfs/02002.pdf public copy], printed p.18 (PDF p.19), family account; printed pp.17, 19–20 (PDF pp.18, 20–21), scope of family histories, James’s papers and later copies. The manuscript histories have not been inspected.</ref>

In his diary entry of 14 August 1858 at Rajkot, James described a voluntary payment to the Crawfords, corresponding through Mr Doads of Clough. He considered the possibility of an error by his father in dealings with their landlords, although he did not believe the landlord had been wronged. One recipient was Mr W. Crawford. This is a specific landlord and correspondence lead, not a statement that the Crawfords were relatives or that they belonged to James’s later Crawford in-laws. No holding, predecessor or earlier parent is named.<ref name="CrawfordPayment1858">James McClure Glasgow, diary, p.29, 14 August 1858, Rajkot, [https://revjamesmcclureglasgow.blogspot.com/ public transcription]. Remarks about tenant right and changed handwriting are editorial commentary; the original manuscript was not inspected for this review.</ref>

D2003 includes Glasgow-family histories and miscellaneous papers relating to James, but no inspected catalogue description identifies the Doads receipt. Its survival in the collection remains unconfirmed. The detailed list and family volumes may help trace the Bannside origin or identify the landlord dealings; no father for John is established by these descriptions.<ref name="CrawfordD2003Scope" />
A possible identification concerns John Glasco, charged at Bow Street. John Glasco, Esq., said he was an officer on the Staff and was brought before the Bow Street magistrate charged with wounding patrolman John Smith. The reported incident occurred on Tuesday night after the play in Covent Garden; Glasco was committed.<ref>The Times, 2 May 1799, p.3, Public Office, Bow Street; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/32820363/ record].</ref> Allegation and committal are not conviction. Military status is self-reported and unconfirmed; no Irish origin or kin is stated. The identification remains uncertain.

=== Family and possible parents ===

The Racavan memorial names John's son [[Glasgow-1778|William Glasgow]], his daughter [[Glasgow-1779|Jane Armstrong]] and his widow [[McClure-6341|Jane]]. The transcription gives William's death as 1823 aged 22; the separate David Elliott cemetery index reads 1829 aged 22. The conflicting year needs a photograph of the stone, while both readings agree on John dying in 1836 aged 70 and Jane in 1858 aged 85.<ref name="RacavanIndex">David Elliott, ''Antrim Cemetery Records'', Racavan Burying Ground, plot R17-10; Findmypast entries IRE/BMD/D/ANT/202500373 (John, 1836, age 70), IRE/BMD/D/ANT/202500372 (Jane, 1858, age 85), and IRE/BMD/D/ANT/202500374 (William, 1829, age 22).</ref>

The Crawford and Glasgow family-paper description names [[Glasgow-1780|James McClure Glasgow]], born near Clough in 1805, as the third of seven children of John Glasgow of Bannside and Jean or Jane McClure. It does not name John's parents. The earlier elder [[Glasgow-3967|James Glasgow]] and the Larne family remain wider comparisons; no named father is selected for John, and his upstream parentage is unrated.<ref name="CrawfordPapers">PRONI, [https://www.sommemidulster.org/dwd/pdfs/02002.pdf Crawford and Glasgow family papers, D2003/MIC128, public introduction]. The manuscript family histories have not been inspected.</ref>

[[Glasgow-2407|John Glasgow, farmer of Cross]], is probably this John's son, with an individual identity assessment of '''84%'''. His 1865 marriage names his father as John Glasgow, farmer, and his 1874 death places him at Cross aged 65. The elder John's 1836 notice names Cross near Broughshane; the 1862 valuation records a John Glasgow holding in Cross, Ballyclug parish. Exact locality and compatible generation favour this father over [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow of Glenleslie]], who remains an alternative. The record proves the father's name and occupation; identification with this man is inferred, and the holding is not proved to have descended by inheritance. No mother is identified for John-2407 by this argument.<ref name="CrossMarriage1865">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1865/11578/8260226.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, marriage register], John Glasgow and Rachel Grey, 11 September 1865.</ref><ref name="CrossDeath1874">[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/images/deaths_returns/deaths_1874/020673/7253774.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, death register], John Glasgow, 27 January 1874.</ref><ref name="CrossNotice1836">''Belfast Commercial Chronicle'', 10 August 1836, p. 3, deaths column; British Newspaper Archive article BL/0001287/18360810/010. The day is lost in the available OCR; the quoted 28 July requires confirmation on the page image.</ref><ref name="CrossValuation1862">''Griffith's Valuation'', Ballyclug parish, printed 23 January 1862, Cross townland, John Glasgow, lessor Henry Joy Tomb; Findmypast IRE/GRIFF/003/003068/001/1.</ref>

This household is distinct from [[Glasgow-822|John Glasgow of Inishrush and Ohio]], who survived until 1851.
